newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit stays in narrow range vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit stays in narrow range vs dollar.

text.p: The ringgit stayed within a tight range against the dollar in Asian trading on Wednesday, with local exporters' selling again capping the dollar's rise, dealers said.

"The trend has not changed from the last few days. Offshore players were buying the dollar at the lower levels while local corporates were selling at the higher end," said a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur.
Dealers said the ringgit was sandwiched between offshore dollar demand around 2.5145 and local corporate dollar sales around 2.5170.
Dealers said due to a lack of fresh factors, dollar/ringgit would continue to consolidate within its current range.
Dealers said the market was also waiting for the release of Malaysia's April trade data after speculation that it would be in deficit of up to two billion ringgit.
A Reuters poll of nine economists produced an average forecast of a 273.6 million ringgit deficit in April. Malaysia posted a trade surplus of 1.75 billion ringgit in March.
Dealers said market players were also eyeing the May U.S. payrolls data due on Friday.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5160/70 a dollar against 2.5175/85 at the close of Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday.
